full_judgment:
S.K, Sinha J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 7th January, 2010 of a Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 78 of 2007. 

 2. The short facts relevant for the disposal of this petition are that the petitioner instituted Title Suit No. 38 of 2005 in the 3rd Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka for Specific Performance of contract stating, inter alia, that the plaintiff company is a sister concern, of Globe Pharmaceuticals Group of Companies. The defendant No.  4 company obtained loan from the defendant No. 1 Bank and the defendant No. 5 as the Managing Director of the defendant No. 4 company and guarantor of the loan had mortgaged his property with the defendant No. 1 Bank as collateral security. The defendant No. 4 failed to repay the aforesaid loan and accordingly the defendant No. 1 filed Title Suit No.  154 of 1997 in the 3rd Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka against the defendant No. 4 and its Directors for recovery of the said loan and the said suit on transfer to the Court of 1st Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka renumbered as Title Suit No. 275 of 2000. The defendant No. 1 ultimately obtained decree in Title Suit No. 275 of 2000 for Tk. 9,14,00,000/-. 

 4. The defendant Nos. 4 and 5 jointly filed written statement, the added defendant No. 7 filed another written statement and contested the suit. The case of the defendant Nos. 4 and 5 is that when the alleged contract was executed the plaintiff was aware that a Specialized Hospital was running in the suit property as tenant. The defendant No. 1, obtained a decree for a sum of Tk. 9,14,00,000/- in Artha Rin Suit No. 275 of 2000 and on 09.1.2000 by an amicable settlement it was settled that if the judgment debtor paid Tk. 3,50,00,000/- within 30.09.2001, the entire amount would be deemed to have been paid on full satisfaction and in default, the judgment debtor was required to pay Tk. 914,00,000/-. Under the above circumstances, the defendant No. 5 was constrained to offer for sale of the suit property to the plaintiff and there was a tripartite agreement providing that within 17.6.2001, Tk.  40,00,000/- was to be deposited with the Arab Bangladesh Bank in the account of defendant No. 4; Taka-1,00,00,090/- (one crore) was to be deposited within 31.7.2001 and Tk. 3,00,00,000/-(three crore) within 30.9.2001. But the plaintiff failed to make those payments as per schedule. As a result, on 16.6.2002 defendant No. 1 rescinded the contract and the defendant Nos. 1 and 5 jointly on 12.12.2002 published notice for selling the suit property and one Mrs. Jeba Ali purchased the same at Tk. 4,40,00,000/-. Though she paid Tk. 1,50,00,000/- but failed to pay the balance amount, and approached the defendant No. 7 to purchase, who at a time paid Tk. 4,80,00,000/- and purchased the suit property. 

 6. Mr. M. Amirul Islam, the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner contended that the High Court Division erred in law in dismissing the appeal in failing to consider that the tripartite agreement has not been rescinded and since the plaintiff is willing to perform its part of obligation, in the absence of contrary evidence, it is entitled to a decree for specific performance. He further contended that the High Court Division failed to appreciate that the defendant No. 7 did not produce any documentary or oral evidence to prove his possession. Mr. Islam finally contended that in a contract for sale of immovable property time is not intended to be the essence of the contract, the High Court Division, in the premises, erred in law in maintaining the judgment of the trial Court. Mr. Fida M. Kamal and Mr. Syed Amirul Islam, appearing for the caveators, supported the judgment of the High Court Division.
